title: Virtual biotech staffed by 37,000 AI agents found a marker for more successful medicines
key_facts: Stanford team led by James Zou built a 'virtual biotech' of AI agents; lead author Harrison Zhang
37,075 agents read trial registries, papers and press releases in about six hours
Humans checked 100 trials and agreed with the agents about 88% of the time
Drugs aimed at genes active in few cell types were 40% more likely to move from phase 1 to phase 2 and 48% more likely to reach phase 4
Their trials reported side effects 32% lower on average
The result is a link found in past trial records, not proof of cause
The agents ran no lab experiments; their lung cancer and colitis proposals still need testing
quote_evidence: The agents found the pattern in records of trials that already happened, so it's a link, not proof that a narrow target makes a drug work.
The agents didn't run any lab experiments, though.
The code is public on GitHub, so other teams can run the agents themselves.
why_it_matters_hint: Could help drugmakers choose targets before costly trials, but only as a statistical link.
notes: AOL carries Earth.com's own reporting (interviews with Zou cited as told to Earth.com); original Earth.com link not seen, AOL page used. Study journal/preprint not named in text.
